chunks: Ali (peace be upon him) from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Durust, from Abu al-Mu'za, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'If a man dies and leaves behind his paternal aunt and his maternal aunt, then the paternal aunt receives two-thirds and the maternal aunt receives one-third.'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a paternal aunt versus a maternal aunt when both survive the deceased?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific division of the estate between the paternal aunt (ammah) and maternal aunt (khalah) when they are the sole heirs, assigning two-thirds to the former and one-third to the latter. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the strength of the paternal lineage in inheritance distribution, distinguishing it from other schools of thought that may treat them equally or prioritize the maternal side differently. The hadith serves as a key precedent for understanding how *'asabah* (residuary heirs) and *dhawu al-furud* (fixed-share heirs) interact in the absence of closer relatives like parents or siblings.
